ownership_reason: Only the gold sees a match together with its position and the units that follow it in both the CharSequence and the search array; hops 1-4 hold the whole CharSequence and the whole search set and get back one boolean, which cannot be traced back to the match that produced it. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the sibling overload StringUtils.containsAny(CharSequence, char[]) (the facade's original delegate, still called by StringEscapeUtils' CSV escaper) counts a match at a high surrogate only when the following units match too ('ch is a supplementary character'), and an unpaired high surrogate counts as a char of its own; testContainsAnyCharArrayWithSupplementaryChars asserts the same five cases for that overload and passes; StringUtils.contains treats a supplementary character as one unit (testContainsStringWithSupplementaryChars: contains(CharU20000, CharU20001) is false). The gold's javadoc promises whether the CharSequence contains any character in the given set, which U+20000 does not for the set {U+20001}. A one-line filter above the gold that drops the high surrogates from the search set (for example CharSetUtils.delete(searchChars, "\uD800-\uDBFF") at hop 2) passes the existing tests but is not consistent with the path: it breaks hop 2's documented conversion of the search String's characters, and an unpaired high surrogate is then never found (containsAny("\uD840", "\uD840") gives false, where the char[] overload gives true).
